text: A Step Back in Time: Once a Proud Capital in Ancient Sri Lanka

html: Once the second capital of Sri Lanka, Polonnaruwa stands as a testament to the ingenuity and artistry of the island’s medieval civilization. Flourishing between the 11th and 13th centuries, this ancient city boasts well-preserved ruins, impressive architecture, and sacred monuments that reflect the grandeur of Sri Lanka’s royal past.

After the decline of Anuradhapura, King Vijayabahu I made Polonnaruwa his capital, followed by the legendary King Parakramabahu the Great, whose reign marked one of the most prosperous times in Sri Lankan history.

Walking through Polonnaruwa feels like stepping into a living museum. Ancient palaces, towering stupas, and intricate statues stand gracefully amidst lush greenery — a testament to the architectural brilliance and spiritual depth of ancient Sri Lanka.

• Royal Palace of King Parakramabahu
     Once a seven-story marvel, the ruins of this grand palace still evoke awe. Its stone pillars and remaining walls give visitors a glimpse of the royal life that once flourished here.

• Gal Vihara
     This rock temple features four magnificent Buddha statues carved into a single granite rock. The serene reclining Buddha is especially captivating and considered one of Sri Lanka’s finest examples of ancient craftsmanship.

• Vatadage (Circular Relic House)
    A masterpiece of symmetry and devotion, the Vatadage once protected sacred relics of the Buddha. The intricately carved moonstones and guard stones reveal the artistic sophistication of ancient Sinhalese culture

• Parakrama Samudraya (Sea of Parakrama)
     This massive reservoir, built by King Parakramabahu, symbolizes his famous words: “Let not even a drop of rainwater go to the sea without being used for the benefit of the people.” It’s a stunning example of advanced ancient engineering — still serving the region today.

Exploring these historic wonders with our Polonnaruwa and Habarana Safari Tour gives travelers more than just sightseeing — it’s a chance to step into the heart of Sri Lanka’s royal past with the guidance of experienced local experts who bring each monument’s story to life.

text: From Royalty to Untamed Wilderness: Journey to Habarana

html: We combine royalty with wild in our Polonnaruwa and Habarana Safari Tour, as it is a perfect day tour to experience all at once which kind of rare to find in one go. After a morning steeped in history, the journey continues to Habarana, located just about 30 minutes from Polonnaruwa. The change in atmosphere is immediate — from ancient stone ruins to lush jungles and tranquil lakes.

Habarana is known as a gateway to Sri Lanka’s most thrilling wildlife safaris, offering travelers the chance to witness elephants, exotic birds, and breathtaking landscapes up close. It’s also the perfect base for exploring the Minneriya and Kaudulla National Parks, where nature unfolds in its raw, untouched beauty.

The Habarana Safari tour is one of the most unforgettable adventures in Sri Lanka. As you set off in an open 4x4 jeep, the breeze carries the scent of wild grass and distant calls of birds. Every turn of the trail holds a surprise — a family of elephants bathing in a lake, a herd crossing the dusty paths, or a peacock proudly displaying its feathers.

text: What You’ll See on the Habarana Safari

html:
• The Majestic Elephants
     The main highlight of any Habarana safari is the Sri Lankan elephants. During certain months, especially between June and September, visitors can witness “The Gathering” — one of the largest natural elephant congregations in the world at nearby Minneriya National Park.

• Birdwatching Paradise
     Habarana is a haven for bird lovers. From painted storks and pelicans to kingfishers and eagles, the skies are alive with color and sound.
• Leopards, Deer, and Other Wildlife

While elephants steal the spotlight, the park is also home to leopards, deer, monkeys, wild boar, and even crocodiles. Every safari is a new adventure, with nature’s surprises waiting at every corner.
• Scenic Landscapes and Sunsets

As the day ends in our Polonnaruwa and Habarana Safari Tour, the golden hues of the setting sun reflect on the lakes and paddy fields — a sight that leaves travelers speechless. The beauty of Habarana lies not just in its wildlife but in its serene landscapes that soothe the soul.
